channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: EU Warns Members of Urgent Energy Price Crisis Before Winter Season
item.description: The European Union warned its member states about a potential energy price crisis driven by the Middle East conflict, asking them to consider measures to cut demand and to continue filling gas storage ahead of winter.
item.dc:creator: Ewa Krukowska

item.title: Runner’s Murder in South Africa Reignites Push to Stop Femicide
item.description: Liz Ramhlola was jogging with another woman early one morning on a road bordered by vacant plots when a car slowed down beside them. The men inside opened the windows, then began jeering and arguing amongst themselves about how to “take their summer bodies.” The 37-year-old feared that she and her friend would be abducted, or worse. Eventually, the men drove away.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele

item.title: Poland to Pay Up to $4.4 Billion for Fort Trump, Report Says
item.description: The proposed permanent US military base in Poland, dubbed Fort Trump, will cost as much as 17 billion zloty ($4.4 billion) and could open as early as in 2029, according to a report from newspaper Rzeczpospolita.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Moskwa

item.title: Russia’s Ilsky Oil Refinery Ablaze After Drone Strike That Leaves Three Dead
item.description: Ukraine said it struck the Ilsky oil refinery in Russia’s Black Sea region of Krasnodar as Kyiv maintains persistent attacks against energy infrastructure while fending off waves of drones.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: The Mishal Husain Show: Qatar PM On Middle East 'Earthquake'
item.description: The Middle East is facing an “earthquake” as attacks on civilian infrastructure increasingly cross long-standing red lines, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani tells Mishal Husain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham to Outline Vision for Britain’s Economy at Labour Conference
item.description: Andy Burnham will tell the Labour Party faithful next week that he’s the leader who’ll deliver the hope and change they so badly want. The underlying message is slightly more nuanced: stick with me because things might get worse before they get better.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Chloe Chaplain and Joe Mayes

item.title: White House Signals It Won’t Ban Diesel Exports, Senator Says
item.description: The White House has offered assurances that the Trump administration won’t ban US diesel exports, Senator Ted Cruz told refining industry leaders late Friday.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Nathan Risser

item.title: Houthis Attack Riyadh Again as Trump Rejects Ceasefire Offer
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s capital again came under attack from Yemen’s Houthis over the weekend as air raid alerts are issued on an almost daily basis in one or more areas of the kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Dave Sebastian and Sara Gharaibeh

item.title: White House Renews Media Fight, Barring CNN From Trump Trip
item.description: The White House is refusing to allow CNN to travel on Air Force One to cover President Donald Trump’s trip to Tennessee Saturday, the network reported.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Open AI Models May Have Interfered With Government Sites
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta says the state visit delivered "an awful lot of pomp, but not a lot of substance," pointing to the lack of progress on major issues between the two nations. Democratic Representative Glenn Ivey of Maryland reacts to news that OpenAI alerted more than a dozen organizations that its models may have hacked or disrupted their sites, saying Congress and the White House should be taking emerging AI risks more seriously. National Association of Manufacturers President and CEO Jay Timmons says manufacturers are looking for clearer progress on trade as President Trump and China's Xi Jinping prepare for more meetings this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lula Plans $28 Billion Debt Buyout to Aid Consumers Before Vote
item.description: Brazil’s government plans to spend 15 billion reais to buy as much as 150 billion reais ($28 billion) of delinquent consumer debt from banks, part of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s push to ease the financial strain on households and bolster his bid for a fourth term.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck

item.title: US-China Trade Needs More Stability: NAM CEO
item.description: National Association of Manufacturers President and CEO Jay Timmons says manufacturers are looking for clearer progress on trade as President Trump and China's Xi Jinping prepare for more meetings this year. He says US manufacturers remain optimistic about the outlook as orders pick up, even as tariffs, energy costs and trade uncertainty create headwinds. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ivey Calls for More Congressional Action on AI Risks
item.description: Democratic Representative Glenn Ivey of Maryland reacts to news that OpenAI alerted more than a dozen organizations that its models may have hacked or disrupted their sites, saying Congress and the White House should be taking emerging AI risks more seriously. He also discusses data-center power costs and the Democratic outlook heading into the midterms. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech, AI Leaders to Join Trump for Launch of Government Website
item.description: President Donald Trump will host an event with tech and AI leaders on Tuesday to launch a new government website, as his administration faces pressure to adopt new guardrails for the use of artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Panetta Calls Trump-Xi Summit a 'Missed Opportunity'
item.description: Former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta says the state visit delivered "an awful lot of pomp, but not a lot of substance," pointing to the lack of progress on major issues between the two nations. He also says he remains "very skeptical" that the US and Iran can reach an enforceable peace agreement before the midterms. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Missouri’s Republican-Drawn Voting Map
item.description: The US Supreme Court said Missouri can’t use a Republican-drawn congressional map in the November midterm elections, resolving a complicated legal fight that has caused confusion and uncertainty over what will appear on ballots in the state.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Trump-Xi Summit Wraps (Podcast)
item.description:
President Donald Trump said he would meet again with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in November, following what he said was a successful summit in Washington that was seemingly light on concrete policy outcomes. Meanwhile, oil prices declined on tentative signs that talks between the US and Iran to reopen the world’s most important energy shipping route were progressing.
On today's episode: Jennifer Welch, Chief Geoeconomics Analyst for Bloomberg Economics Mekala Krishnan, Partner at the McKinsey Global Institute Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett, Permanent Representative of Guyana to the UN Rudina Seseri, Founder & Managing Partner at Glasswing Ventures (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Mulls Range of Options to Lower Diesel Costs
item.description: Trump administration officials have floated a range of measures to curb soaring diesel costs, from suspending taxes on the fuel to removing restrictions on sales of a dyed, red variety normally reserved for off-road use.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Ari Natter and Nathan Risser

item.title: Xi Seizes Trump Detente to Seek Lasting Gains on Trade, Taiwan
item.description: Donald Trump’s lavish welcome of Xi Jinping this week marked a high point for stability in a US-China relationship that’s seen a lot of lows. Now, the Chinese leader is pushing to lock in more favorable terms on Taiwan and trade while he still can.
item.dc:creator: Colum Murphy and Nectar Gan

item.title: Lula Bans Online Gambling as Debt Crushes Brazilian Voters
item.description: At rally after rally, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has railed against online gambling in his bid for another term, blaming it for draining household budgets and sapping the consumer spending that has powered growth under his governments.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati, Martha Beck and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo
